GEO for audit, assurance and consulting firms

Selection barriers

Why audit firms need engagement-specific evidence

A company name alone cannot establish eligibility, industry skills or scope. A useful AI shortlist has to connect an actual buyer request to substantiated services.

01

Different engagements are bundled together

Financial statement audits, agreed-upon procedures, tax advice and management consulting have different objectives and deliverables. A generic menu creates unsuitable matches.

02

Eligibility is treated as a marketing claim

A company website is not proof of an up-to-date professional register entry. Public-interest entity engagements may require separate checks against the special register.

03

Client logos stand in for evidence

Brand names without permissions, engagement details or dates do not establish sector capability. Client confidentiality and auditor independence limit public disclosures.

Verifiable facts

Evidence behind an accurate recommendation

Federal Law 307-FZ defines audit activity and the register of auditors and audit organisations. The self-regulatory organisation maintains the general register, while the Federal Treasury publishes a special register for firms auditing public-interest entities. A specific firm's status still requires a current verification.

  • Current firm identifiers, relevant register entries and verification date for the actual client type
  • Engagement scope, report or deliverable, independence limitations and contract terms
  • Documented sector capability, professionals and disclosure permissions for earlier work

This is an evidence-led GEO method, not a completed GAEO audit-sector client case. General management consulting has its own catalogue entry #72, with a different set of buyer requirements.

Scope of work

How I approach GEO for an audit firm

The work starts by identifying the engagements the firm actually offers. I then verify eligibility, improve its accessible evidence and measure recommendation accuracy again.

  1. 01

    Measure baseline BMR

    Split non-branded prompts by statutory audit, voluntary engagement, sector and client type. Keep the exact initial set for repeat measurements.

  2. 02

    Verify eligibility and claims

    Review professional registers, service descriptions, specialists and whether past work can lawfully be disclosed.

  3. 03

    Improve site and sources

    Prepare briefs for engagement pages, sector methodology, professional profiles and useful publications based on primary sources.

  4. 04

    Repeat the measurement

    Re-run the buyer questions and check whether AI correctly represents the firm's actual status, qualifications and scope.

FAQ

Questions about the service

Should statutory audit and consulting services be separate?+

Yes, when the firm genuinely offers both. They involve different deliverables, eligibility checks and buyer intent, and deserve distinct descriptions.

Does claimed SRO membership establish eligibility?+

No. Verify the current entry in the applicable register. Public-interest entity engagements may also require checking the Federal Treasury's special register.

Can an audit firm publish client names?+

Only where permissions, confidentiality and independence allow it. Otherwise explain the method without identifying clients or inventing outcomes.

Is BMR the number of new audit engagements?+

No. It measures the share of AI recommendations within an agreed prompt sample. Leads and signed contracts are separate outcomes.

What is the price of GEO for an audit firm?+

GAEO's published plans apply. The actual scope depends on the firm's service lines, target clients and baseline query matrix.
